title: Blockbuster passes on buying Netflix
decision: In 2000 Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph named a price of $50 million for Netflix, a money-losing DVD-by-mail start-up, at Blockbuster's Dallas headquarters. Blockbuster declined. The details of the meeting are disputed: Randolph recalls a sale pitch and a barely hidden laugh, Hastings recalls curiosity, and Antioco says there were no serious talks and he only greeted the guests.
hook: In 2000, two founders offered to sell their money-losing start-up to the biggest video chain in America for $50 million. The answer was no. Today that start-up is worth hundreds of billions, and the chain is down to one store in Oregon.
